subtype: Approach: treating sport as reward only after study [Pitfall]
passage: Wei made a rule in September in Lima: football only after all revision is finished. It sounded strict and fair. But revision has no end, so each evening it ran to ten o'clock and the boots stayed in the bag. By week three Wei had not kicked a ball for eleven days. Study felt heavier and slower, and reading the same paragraph twice became normal. Camila, from the team, messaged, "We miss you. You look tired." Wei looked at the message for a long time. Mood down, focus worse, and an hour on the pitch might have been the very thing that helped. Wei did not reply that night.

qa.q: How many days had Wei gone without football?
qa.a: Wei had gone eleven days without kicking a ball.

qa.q: How did Wei feel on reading Camila's message?
qa.a: Low and worn out, since Wei stared at it for a long time and did not reply.

qa.q: What alternative could work better for Wei?
qa.a: Schedule football at a fixed time and study in set blocks, because sport helps focus and revision otherwise never ends.

qa.q: How might Camila see Wei's absence?
qa.a: With concern, since Camila messaged that the team misses Wei and Wei looks tired.

grounding: A student makes football depend on finishing all revision, so study runs late, sport disappears, mood falls and concentration worsens.

subtype: Approach: treating sport as reward only after study [Pitfall]
passage: At the school football ground, Sunaina Ma'am marked the register: Parveen absent again, the sixth practice in a row. She found Parveen in the library at half past five, head down on her Chemistry book. "You were my best defender. What happened?" "I made a rule," Parveen said. "Football only after all my revision is done. It was supposed to make me study faster." "Has it?" Parveen shook her head. "The revision never finishes. So I never go. And now I read the same page five times and nothing goes in." She rubbed her eyes. "I'm grumpy at home too." Sunaina Ma'am sat down beside her. "Football isn't the prize at the end. It might be what keeps your head working."

qa.q: How many practices in a row had Parveen missed?
qa.a: The sixth practice in a row.

qa.q: How is Parveen feeling in the library?
qa.a: She feels tired, grumpy and discouraged, reading the same page five times without anything going in.

qa.q: What would you change first in Parveen's rule?
qa.a: Give football a fixed slot, such as two evenings a week, instead of making it wait for finished revision, since the exercise may help her focus.

qa.q: How does Sunaina Ma'am see the rule?
qa.a: She sees it backfiring and thinks football may be helping Parveen's concentration rather than competing with it.

grounding: Shows a student making football depend on finishing revision, so sport disappears and her mood and focus get worse.

subtype: Approach: treating sport as reward only after study [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Kishore Sir,
I'm sorry I haven't come to Saturday football for a month. In January I decided I'd only let myself play once all my weekly revision was done, as a reward. It sounded smart. But the revision list never ended. Every Saturday there was one more chapter, so I stayed home. Now I'm studying more hours than ever and getting less done. I get headaches by evening and snap at my mother over nothing. My marks in the last test actually dropped. My friend said running around used to be the only time my head went quiet. I think she's right. Can I come back this Saturday? I'll keep the revision, but football will be a fixed slot, not a prize.
Kashish

qa.q: How long has Kashish missed Saturday football?
How has Kashish been feeling since stopping football?
qa.a: Kashish feels irritable and worn out, with evening headaches and snapping at home, and frustrated that more hours bring less done.

qa.q: Why is a fixed slot better than football as a reward?
qa.a: A fixed slot guarantees the exercise that clears Kashish's head, while a reward that depends on finishing never arrives when the list keeps growing.

qa.q: How might Kishore Sir feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Kishore Sir may feel glad the player wants to come back, and concerned about the headaches and the dropped marks.

grounding: A student's letter shows football made a reward for finished revision, sport vanishing, and mood and concentration falling.
